output.summary: The admitted-patient length-of-stay rise is almost entirely boarding (about 3.0 of 3.2 hours). It began in March 2026, when the hospitalist rounding change delayed medical-ward discharges. Surgical wards, which weren't affected by the change, stayed flat. RN hours per visit, vacancy and grid compliance were flat. Visits, acuity, beds and occupancy were also flat. The 4 West pilot, with huddle days set by a pre-made schedule, shows earlier discharges cut boarding. ED nurses are overloaded by holding admitted patients. Extend the huddle. Don't fund travel nurses by deferring case managers. Don't pause the huddle. The evening bed-cleaning cut is unproven.
